item.title: Sqwod Daily — Thursday, 22 October 2026
item.description: Club Pilates is adding a circuit-style class and refreshing studios system-wide as it approaches 1500 locations, plus Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym sets a December opening.
item.content:encoded:
Thursday, 22 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Thursday, 22 October 2026 · Weekday
Club Pilates is adding a circuit-style class and refreshing studios system-wide as it approaches 1500 locations, plus Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym sets a December opening.
— Sqwod
Connect the dots
Club Pilates on growing to 1500 locations without losing what works
Tianna Strateman, brand president of Club Pilates, spoke with Club Solutions editor Taylor Gabhart on the Club Solutions podcast about how the brand is evolving as it approaches its 20th anniversary and 1500th location. The brand is introducing a circuit-style class format, driven by two signals Strateman identified: the rise of strength training and the growing use of GLP-1 medications. At the same time, Club Pilates is rolling out studio refreshes across its entire system, designed to limit disruption for franchisees and protect the member experience.
For studio owners, the approach offers a practical model: Strateman described how the brand chose which key performance indicators to track when launching changes across a large system, and how the physical updates were structured to keep return on investment clear for individual operators. The lesson is that innovation tied to measurable signals and tracked against specific metrics is easier to justify and manage than change for its own sake.
The rundown
01
Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym Set to Open in December
Mark Wahlberg's Municipal Gym is scheduled to open in December, with a focus on longevity, blood work and recovery. No further location or pricing details were confirmed in the source.
Source: Athletech News →
02
ACISO Consulting adds four staff across consulting, marketing and digital
ACISO Consulting, a fitness business consulting firm, has hired four people: Florian Otto as a consultant covering the Aachen region and German postcode area 5, Schirin Mameghani in online marketing, Nadya Ramzy as marketing manager, and Fabian Ackermann supporting digital processes. The hires were announced in October 2026. Studios working with ACISO can expect more regional coverage and expanded marketing support.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Club Pilates president explains push to 1500 locations and new class format
Tianna Strateman, brand president of Club Pilates, spoke with Club Solutions editor Taylor Gabhart on the Club Solutions podcast to discuss how the brand, approaching its 20th anniversary, is adding a circuit-style class format and rolling out studio refreshes across its system as it nears 1500 locations. Strateman said two industry signals, the rise of strength training and GLP-1 use, pointed the brand toward the new class offering. She also covered how the studio refreshes were designed to limit disruption for franchisees and which key performance indicators the brand tracks to measure a system-wide launch.
Source: Club Solutions →
04
HCM Invest launches in London on 21 October 2026
Health Club Management held the first HCM Invest event in London on 21 October 2026, bringing together investors, operators, entrepreneurs and advisers to explore investment and growth opportunities across fitness, health and wellness. Studio owners and coaches looking for funding or partnerships may find this kind of dedicated investor forum a useful channel to watch.
Source: Health Club Management →
05
Careerz Group launches AI coaching tool built on workforce assessment data
Careerz Group, based in Okemos, Michigan, announced Careerz Coach AI on October 20, 2026. The tool lets managers ask questions about people and workplace situations and receive guidance drawn from assessment data already collected through their workforce program, including DISC, JPTI, Motivators and emotional intelligence assessments. Coaches who use structured assessments with clients or staff may find this approach, connecting stored assessment results to real-time questions, a useful model for making assessment data more actionable day to day.
Source: markets.businessinsider.com →
06
Global Wellness Institute: Lack of Belonging Is a Major Driver of Workplace Stress
The Global Wellness Institute has published a piece arguing that workplace culture, not standalone programs, is the foundation of employee mental wellbeing. It identifies lack of belonging as a large cause of workplace stress, alongside pressure from leaders, self-imposed overwork, and exclusion by colleagues. For coaches and studio owners who employ staff, the piece suggests that culture built by leaders matters more than any single wellness offering.
Source: Global Wellness Institute →
Stat
1500
Club Pilates locations as the brand approaches its 20th anniversary
The scale shows how far a single modality can travel when it is franchised consistently, and sets the context for why system-wide launches require careful measurement.

item.title: Sqwod Daily — Wednesday, 21 October 2026
item.description: The ACSM has ranked wearable technology as the world's top fitness trend for 2027, while Fitness On Demand expands its digital library and Unravel Health secures new funding.
item.content:encoded:
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Wednesday, 21 October 2026 · Weekday
The ACSM has ranked wearable technology as the world's top fitness trend for 2027, while Fitness On Demand expands its digital library and Unravel Health secures new funding.
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
Unravel Health
 €2.5M
raised to launch the Micro Lab, an at-home saliva-based hormone testing device shipping in 2027
Connect the dots
ACSM ranks wearable technology the top global fitness trend for 2027
The American College of Sports Medicine published its 21st annual fitness trend survey on 21 October 2026. More than 1,400 fitness professionals rated 50 potential trends. Wearable technology came first, followed by mobile fitness apps and balance, flow and core training. The ACSM releases this ranking each year to show which services and tools are drawing the most attention across the industry internationally.
For coaches and studio owners, the top-ten list is a practical reference point. If wearables and mobile apps are leading globally, clients are likely already tracking their own data. Knowing the ranking helps you decide which tools and services to prioritise or promote in the coming year.
The rundown
01
ACSM names wearable technology the top global fitness trend for 2027
The American College of Sports Medicine published its 21st annual fitness trend survey on 21 October 2026. More than 1,400 fitness professionals rated 50 potential trends, placing wearable technology first, followed by mobile fitness apps and balance, flow and core training. Coaches and studio owners can use the top-ten ranking to judge which services and tools are drawing the most attention internationally.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
02
Fitness On Demand adds 99 Mvmnt workouts to its digital library
Fitness On Demand, a commercial fitness platform serving studios, gyms and wellness operators, announced a content partnership with Mvmnt, a digital fitness platform, on 14 October 2026 in Minneapolis. The deal adds 99 Mvmnt workouts covering strength, cardio, boxing, dance, yoga, Pilates, mobility and meditation to Fitness On Demand's existing library of more than 1,800 workouts, available across in-facility screens and mobile touchpoints. Studio and gym owners can broaden their programming offer without hiring more instructors or adding a separate app.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
03
ØRA Wellness Studio raises over €1,000 for Breast Cancer Awareness
ØRA Wellness Studio in Athlone, Ireland, raised over €1,000 at its Pink Wellness Morning, organised by studio owner Aishling Croughan and life coach Libby Hayes. The event brought women together for gentle movement, breathwork, coffee and cake, with support from local businesses including Mary's SuperValu Athlone, A Room in Bloom and Sláinte Coffee Shop. The event shows how studios can partner with local businesses and community figures to run charity events that build connection and generate goodwill.
Source: Westmeath Independent →
04
Unravel Health Raises €2.5M for At-Home Hormone Testing Device
Women's hormone monitoring company Unravel Health has raised €2.5 million to launch the Micro Lab, an at-home device that reads estradiol and other biomarkers from saliva in minutes. The device ships in 2027, with plans to add more hormones and expand into men's health. Coaches who work with clients on hormonal health, such as perimenopause or cycle-based training, may eventually have access to daily, lab-grade data rather than relying on single blood test snapshots.
Source: Fitt Insider →
Stat
1,800
workouts in Fitness On Demand's library before the Mvmnt partnership
Fitness On Demand already held more than 1,800 workouts; the addition of 99 Mvmnt sessions covering strength, cardio, boxing, dance, yoga, Pilates, mobility and meditation gives operators a broader programming range without adding equipment or staff.

item.title: Sqwod Daily — Tuesday, 20 October 2026
item.description: PureGym has paid £235 million for a Swiss fitness business, while RockSalt Pilates appoints a franchise veteran to lead an 84-location rollout.
item.content:encoded:
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Tuesday, 20 October 2026 · Weekday
PureGym has paid £235 million for a Swiss fitness business, while RockSalt Pilates appoints a franchise veteran to lead an 84-location rollout.
— Sqwod
Money movement
⇄  Acquired
PureGym
 £235m
acquired a Swiss fitness business
The rundown
01
PureGym buys Swiss fitness business for £235m
PureGym has acquired a Swiss fitness business in a deal worth £235 million.
Source: Irish Legal News →
02
Alexander Sosa opens his 20th Sports Club with €5m investment in Hamburg
Entrepreneur Alexander Sosa opened his 20th Sports Club location in Hamburg-Poppenbüttel in October 2026, celebrating with around 400 guests. The new 5,000-square-metre fitness and wellness facility was converted from a former electronics store at a cost of around five million euros. The project shows that large-scale conversion of retail space into fitness facilities remains a viable route for operators looking to expand in established urban areas.
Source: fitness MANAGEMENT →
03
Jazzercise Founder Judi Sheppard Missett to Enter HFA Hall of Fame in 2027
The Health & Fitness Association will induct Judi Sheppard Missett, founder and executive chair of Jazzercise, into its Hall of Fame on March 10, 2027, during the opening night of The HFA Show 2027 in Las Vegas. Missett built Jazzercise from a class of 15 women into a global dance fitness company over more than five decades. HFA Interim President and CEO Greta Wagner said Missett changed how millions of people experience fitness and created entrepreneurship opportunities for generations of women.
Source: Health & Fitness Association →
04
RockSalt Pilates Hires Franchise Veteran as COO With 84 Locations in Development
Music-driven Pilates brand RockSalt Pilates has appointed Stephanie Knepp, a franchise veteran, as its new chief operating officer. The brand has 84 locations in development, including sites in the UAE. Studio owners considering franchise growth can watch how an experienced franchise operator shapes a scaled rollout at a boutique concept.
Source: Athletech News →
Stat
84
RockSalt Pilates locations in development
Having 84 sites in development, including locations in the UAE, shows how quickly a boutique Pilates brand can scale through franchising once it brings in experienced operational leadership.

✓ Try: Before hiring for a senior operations role, write a one-page document listing the three biggest process problems in your business: it gives any new hire a clear brief and saves onboarding time.

item.title: Sqwod Daily — Monday, 19 October 2026
item.description: Today: an Amsterdam startup raises €1 million to replace patchwork gym software, a Canadian Lagree brand heads to California, and a German briefing on insurer-funded courses.
item.content:encoded:
Monday, 19 October 2026 View online →
DAILY
The fitness industry, decoded — in five minutes.
Monday, 19 October 2026 · Weekday
Today: an Amsterdam startup raises €1 million to replace patchwork gym software, a Canadian Lagree brand heads to California, and a German briefing on insurer-funded courses.
— Sqwod
Money movement
▲  Raise
Huppa
 €1M
pre-seed round for an all-in-one platform for gyms, CrossFit boxes and studios
Connect the dots
Huppa wants to replace the patchwork of studio software
Huppa, an Amsterdam startup founded in 2024 by two gym owners, has raised €1 million in pre-seed funding. Its platform combines member management, class scheduling, payments, financial reporting and automation in one system, connects to Mollie, Urban Sports Club and ClassPass, and charges by the number of active customers. The founders say many gyms and studios still run on outdated software, spend too much time on admin and miss chances to grow revenue because their data is spread across tools.
For a studio owner, the takeaway is practical: every separate tool you pay for is another login, another export and another place where member data can go missing. Whether or not you look at Huppa, it is worth knowing exactly how many systems your business runs on and what they cost together.
The rundown
01
Huppa raises €1M to build one platform for running a gym
Amsterdam startup Huppa has raised €1 million in pre-seed funding for software that combines member management, scheduling, payments and reporting for gyms, CrossFit boxes and studios. It was founded in 2024 by two gym owners and charges by the number of active customers.
Source: EU-Startups →
02
Reformd plans the world's largest Lagree studio in California
Toronto's Reformd, owned by Sweat and Tonic, will open a studio in Calabasas in January 2027 with 37 Lagree machines and six recovery rooms. The recovery services, including cryotherapy and compression therapy, will be open to people who do not take classes.
Source: Athletech News →
03
DSSV briefing on insurer-funded prevention courses, 19 November
Germany's fitness operators' association, the DSSV, is holding an online briefing on 19 November on its courses Kraft Aktiv and Cardio-Fitness. Both are free for members and certified so German studios can bill them to health insurers.
Source: DSSV →
Policy watch
Germany: briefing on insurer-funded prevention courses, 19 November
The DSSV is holding an online briefing on 19 November (12:30 to 13:30) on its prevention courses Kraft Aktiv and Cardio-Fitness. Both are free for DSSV members and certified so studios can bill them to German health insurers.
Stat
126,000
bookings at Reformd's Toronto flagship since June 2025
That is the track record Reformd is taking to California, according to the company.
Sqwod recs
✓ Track: Check your class fill rate every week: booked spots divided by available spots. It shows which time slots to grow and which to cut.
✓ Try: Ask new members on their first visit how they found you, and log the answer. After a month you will know which marketing actually brings people in.
